title: SADL: A Size-Adaptive Decision Layer for Chronic Stroke Lesion Segmentation in ISLES 2026
mechanism: A decision layer fitted on out-of-fold predictions: per-size-bucket thresholds, pruning components by size and peak probability, and a never-empty rescue.
adaptation: Hysteresis-like crack rule: keep a weak component if its peak probability passes its size-bucket threshold; rescue rule for cells where the model outputs nothing (E1 half-cut cells). Fit on CV folds or val + F51 only.
min_experiment: Arm: SADL-style layer on 5-seed ensemble maps. Baseline: ensemble at argmax and with logit bias. Metric: test / E1 relF1@2 and component recall < 20 px. Kill: no gain >= 0.005 relF1@2 on both sets.
evidence: Site-disjoint 91-case holdout: Dice 0.732, lesion F1 0.746, PR-AUC 0.843; bootstrap p = 0.024 vs a single member; gain largest for small lesions.
prior_overlap: Overlaps logit bias and per-module thresholds only in spirit; component-level peak-prob pruning and rescue untested.
